shift.title: People ask ChatGPT before they ask Google.
shift.subtitle: That changes what "being found online" actually means. Three things I see over and over when I check how professionals show up to AI:

points.title: Invisible
points.desc: Not mentioned at all — older or more-reviewed profiles win by default, regardless of who's actually better.

points.title: Misrepresented
points.desc: Mentioned, but with wrong details — an old address, a past employer, a qualification that's no longer current.

points.title: Fragmented
points.desc: The website alone isn't enough. What matters is whether it agrees with Google Business, LinkedIn, and the directories AI actually trusts.

shift.closing: That's the gap I close: making you findable, and correctly described, when it counts.

items.q: How long does a site take?
items.a: A single-page showcase site takes 1–2 weeks from deposit to launch. Multi-page sites take 2–4 weeks depending on complexity.

items.q: Can I update the content myself?
items.a: Yes. I'll hand over the GitHub repo and a plain-English guide. If you'd rather not touch code, I can make changes for a small hourly fee.

No. You pay once and that's it. The only ongoing cost is your domain (~$20/year). Hosting on Vercel is free for sites like yours. AI visibility monitoring is the one optional recurring service, and it's entirely your call.

items.q: Do you provide photos or copy?
items.a: I don't do photography or copywriting — you'll need to supply those. I can advise on what works best and recommend free stock photo sites.

items.q: How long is the bug support?
items.a: 30 days from launch. If something breaks that I caused, I fix it free. After 30 days, changes are quoted at my hourly rate.

items.q: Can you guarantee AI will recommend me?
items.a: No, and anyone who promises that is overselling. What I can do is build the foundation that makes you eligible and correctly represented — the rest depends on reviews, competition, and factors outside anyone's full control.

items.q: Why are you cheaper than an agency?
items.a: I do this on the side to fund travel. No office, no account managers, no overhead. You get agency-level work at a fraction of the price.
